subject: English
title: Arjun and Mitthu Learn Names
hook: Discover naming words — the names of all the things around us!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A curious 6-year-old learning to name things

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A parrot who loves knowing names of everything

image.alt: Arjun and Mitthu Learn Names — Naming Words

slides.title: What's Your Name?
slides.storyContext: Arjun sits on the grass with his friend Mitthu. 'I'm Arjun. That's my name!' he says proudly. Mitthu chirps, 'And I'm Mitthu! Names are special words we use to call things and people. They're called naming words, or nouns!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Naming words are the names of things.

slides.title: What is a Naming Word?
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains the idea simply. 'A naming word is a special word that tells us the NAME of something.'

points.label: Definition
points.text: A naming word (noun) is a word that tells us the name of a person, animal, place, or thing.

points.label: Examples
points.text: Boy, girl, dog, cat, park, tree, ball, book — these all NAME something.

slides.inSimpleWords: Naming words are names of anything you can think of.

image.alt: What is a Naming Word? — Naming Words

slides.title: Names of People
slides.storyContext: Arjun's mom comes outside. 'I'm Priya!' she waves. Grandma joins them. 'I'm Sudha!' she smiles. Mitthu sings, 'Arjun, Priya, Sudha — all naming words! People have names. Boy, girl, man, woman — these are also naming words that tell us what kind of person!'

points.label: People names
points.text: Arjun, Priya, Sudha, boy, girl, man, woman

slides.inSimpleWords: Names of people are naming words.

slides.title: People Names in Detail
slides.storyContext: Mitthu points to different people. 'Look! That's a boy. There's a girl. A woman. A man. A baby. A teacher. Each person can be called by their special name or by what they are.'

points.label: Person names
points.text: Arjun, Priya, Sudha (special names)

points.label: Person types
points.text: Boy, girl, man, woman, baby, teacher, doctor, friend

example.problem: What naming words can you use for your mother?
example.solution: Her special name (like Priya), or the naming word 'mother', 'mom', 'woman'

slides.inSimpleWords: Every person has a special name and a type name.

image.alt: People Names in Detail — Naming Words

slides.title: Names of Animals
slides.storyContext: A dog runs past, wagging its tail. 'That's a dog!' says Arjun. Mitthu nods. 'Dog, cat, parrot, elephant, lion — animal names! And look — a cow in that field! Cow, buffalo, horse, sheep — all naming words for animals!'

points.label: Animal names
points.text: Dog, cat, parrot, lion, cow, buffalo, horse, bird

points.label: Farm animals
points.text: Cow, buffalo, horse, sheep, pig, goat, hen, duck

points.label: Wild animals
points.text: Lion, tiger, elephant, zebra, giraffe, bear, fox, wolf

example.problem: What's the naming word for this?
example.solution: Dog! Or cat, bird, lion — names of animals

slides.inSimpleWords: Names of animals are naming words.

slides.title: Animal Naming Game
slides.storyContext: Mitthu says, 'Let's play! I will make sounds. You say the animal name!' Mitthu barks, meows, neighs, and roars. Arjun laughs and says: 'Dog! Cat! Horse! Lion!'

points.label: Animal examples
points.text: Cat, pig, duck, snake, fish, monkey, turtle, rabbit

example.problem: What naming words are for animals that say 'moo' and 'baa'?
example.solution: Cow and sheep! Each animal has a naming word.

slides.inSimpleWords: Every animal has a naming word.

slides.title: Names of Places
slides.storyContext: Arjun points around him. 'Mitthu, we're in the park!' Mitthu agrees, 'Park! And I see school over there. And a hospital. Park, school, hospital, home, market — these are naming words for places where we go!'

points.label: Place names
points.text: Park, school, home, market, hospital, library, city, village

points.label: Indoor places
points.text: Home, school, hospital, library, kitchen, bedroom, room

points.label: Outdoor places
points.text: Park, garden, playground, market, beach, mountain, river, field

slides.inSimpleWords: Names of places are naming words.

slides.title: Places We Know
slides.storyContext: Mitthu asks Arjun, 'Where do you go every day? What are the names of those places?'

points.label: My places
points.text: Home, school, park, market, temple, hospital, library, playground

example.problem: Where do you go to learn? What is the naming word?
example.solution: School! You might also say classroom, library, or school building.

slides.inSimpleWords: Every place has a naming word.

slides.title: Names of Things
slides.storyContext: Arjun picks up a ball. 'Ball!' he says. Mitthu looks around. 'Yes! And tree, flower, bench, water, sun, moon, cloud — all naming words for things we can see or touch!'

points.label: Thing names
points.text: Ball, tree, flower, book, pen, table, house, car

points.label: Small things
points.text: Pen, pencil, coin, seed, button, leaf, drop, grain

points.label: Big things
points.text: Tree, house, mountain, cloud, sun, moon, river, field

example.problem: Name five things you see.
example.solution: Ball, tree, flower, bench, cloud (all naming words)

slides.inSimpleWords: Names of things we can see are naming words.

slides.title: Things Around Me
slides.storyContext: Arjun walks around his home and points at everything. 'Table! Chair! Window! Door! Cup! Plate! Bed! These are all naming words for things in my house!'

points.label: Household things
points.text: Table, chair, bed, door, window, cup, plate, spoon, fork

points.label: School things
points.text: Desk, pencil, book, notebook, bench, board, eraser, ruler

example.problem: What are five naming words for things in your bedroom?
example.solution: Bed, pillow, window, lamp, door (or any five things you see)

slides.inSimpleWords: Everyday objects all have naming words.

slides.title: Names of Actions... and No!
slides.storyContext: Arjun jumps up. 'Wait, Mitthu! Is jump a naming word?' Mitthu shakes his head. 'No! Jump, run, play, eat — those are action words, not naming words. Naming words are for things, people, places, and animals. Action words are for what we do!'

points.label: Remember
points.text: Naming words = names; Not action words = what we do

slides.inSimpleWords: Naming words name things, not actions.

image.alt: Names of Actions... and No! — Naming Words

slides.title: NOT Naming Words
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'Some words are NOT naming words. They describe things or tell us what people do. Let me show you!'

points.label: Action words (verbs)
points.text: Jump, run, walk, eat, play, sleep, sing — these show ACTIONS, not names.

points.label: Describing words (adjectives)
points.text: Big, small, red, happy, fast, slow — these tell us HOW something is, not what it's CALLED.

example.problem: Is the word 'happy' a naming word?
example.solution: No! 'Happy' tells us how someone feels, not what they are called. It's a describing word, not a naming word.

slides.inSimpleWords: Naming words name things. Action and describing words do NOT name things.

slides.title: Find the Naming Word
slides.storyContext: Mitthu asks a game: 'I say words. You tell me if it's a naming word! Cat... dog... run... tree... happy... book... jump!' Arjun shouts: 'Cat, dog, tree, book are naming words! Run, jump, happy are not!'

points.label: Test yourself
points.text: Cat ✓, run ✗, dog ✓, play ✗, school ✓

example.problem: Is the word happy a naming word?
example.solution: No! It's a describing word, not a name

slides.inSimpleWords: Naming words name things — people, places, animals, objects.

image.alt: Find the Naming Word — Naming Words

slides.title: Naming Word or Not? Practice
slides.storyContext: Mitthu and Arjun play a sorting game. Mitthu says a word, and Arjun puts it in the RIGHT or WRONG pile.

points.label: NAMING WORDS
points.text: Boy, apple, table, car, sister, parrot

points.label: NOT naming words
points.text: Jump, red, happy, run, play, big

example.problem: Sort these: cat, sing, park, funny, teacher, sleep
example.solution: Naming words: cat, park, teacher. Not naming words: sing, funny, sleep

slides.inSimpleWords: Ask: 'Does this word NAME something?' If yes, it's a naming word.

image.alt: Naming Word or Not? Practice — Naming Words

slides.title: Little Words, Big Naming
slides.storyContext: Grandma brings a small notebook. 'Notebook, pencil, paper — names of things!' She writes Arjun's name. 'Even very small things have names. Ant, grain, seed, drop — even the tiny ones have naming words!'

points.label: Even small things
points.text: Ant, seed, drop, grain — all have naming words

slides.inSimpleWords: Everything has a naming word, big or small.

image.alt: Little Words, Big Naming — Naming Words

slides.title: Singular and Plural Naming Words
slides.storyContext: Mitthu points at things differently. 'One book. Two BOOKS. One cat. Three CATS. When there's more than one, the naming word changes!'

points.label: Singular (one)
points.text: Book, cat, ball, tree, boy, girl, dog, pen

points.label: Plural (more than one)
points.text: Books, cats, balls, trees, boys, girls, dogs, pens

points.label: Make plural
points.text: Usually add 's' or 'es' to the singular word.

example.problem: Write the plural of: boy, tree, box, glass
example.solution: Boys, trees, boxes, glasses (we add 'es' to words ending in 'x' or 's')

slides.inSimpleWords: One book, many books. Plural naming words tell us there are more than one.

image.alt: Singular and Plural Naming Words — Naming Words

slides.title: One or Many?
slides.storyContext: Arjun counts things in his garden. 'One flower. Two flowers. Three flowers. One butterfly. Five butterflies!'

points.label: Singular examples
points.text: Flower, butterfly, apple, boy, dog

points.label: Plural examples
points.text: Flowers, butterflies, apples, boys, dogs

example.problem: Make these plural: girl, house, hand, toy
example.solution: Girls, houses, hands, toys

slides.inSimpleWords: Add 's' to make a naming word plural (meaning more than one).

slides.title: Singular to Plural Challenge
slides.storyContext: Mitthu makes a tricky game. 'I say the singular. You say the plural! Book... pen... cat... box... child... man!'

points.label: Regular plurals
points.text: Add 's': books, pens, cats

points.label: Tricky ones
points.text: Box→boxes, child→children, man→men (irregular!)

example.problem: What's the plural of 'box' and 'child'?
example.solution: Boxes (add 'es') and children (completely different—irregular)

slides.inSimpleWords: Most naming words become plural by adding 's'. Some change completely!

image.alt: Singular to Plural Challenge — Naming Words

slides.title: Naming Word Hunt
slides.storyContext: Mitthu and Arjun look around Arjun's home. 'Name everything!' Arjun points: 'Door, window, table, chair, bed, lamp, cup, book!' All naming words!

points.label: Around the house
points.text: Door, window, table, chair, bed, lamp, cup, book, pen, wall, floor, roof

example.problem: What are 10 naming words in your room?
example.solution: Bed, pillow, window, lamp, door, wall, floor, shelf, book, toy (any 10 things)

slides.inSimpleWords: Look around and name everything!

slides.title: Mixed Categories Challenge
slides.storyContext: Mitthu mixes it up. 'Give me one naming word for each: a person, an animal, a place, a thing, and tell me one word that is NOT a naming word!'

points.label: Example
points.text: Person: boy, Animal: cat, Place: school, Thing: pen, NOT naming: run

example.problem: Give examples for: person, animal, place, thing, describing word
example.solution: Person: Arjun, Animal: dog, Place: park, Thing: ball, Describing: happy

slides.inSimpleWords: You've learned all kinds of naming words!

slides.title: Naming Words All Around
slides.storyContext: Mitthu sings a song: 'Naming words, naming words, everywhere I see! Table, dog, and Arjun, and a big blue tree!'

points.label: Count naming words in sentences
points.text: Arjun sees a dog in the park. (Arjun, dog, park=3 naming words)

example.problem: How many naming words in: 'The boy and girl play at school'?
example.solution: Boy, girl, school = 3 naming words

slides.inSimpleWords: Sentences use many naming words!

image.alt: Naming Words All Around — Naming Words

slides.title: Common Naming Words Game
slides.storyContext: Arjun closes his eyes. Mitthu says fast: Pencil! Tree! Boy! Arjun shouts: Naming word! All naming words!
slides.inSimpleWords: Recognizing naming words gets easy!

slides.title: Common Naming Words
slides.storyContext: Mitthu lists the most common ones.

points.label: All types
points.text: Boy, girl, man, woman, dog, cat, bird, home, school, book, pen, tree

example.problem: List 5 naming words
example.solution: Boy, dog, home, pen, tree

slides.inSimpleWords: These naming words you use every day!

slides.title: Master Challenge
slides.storyContext: Mitthu: Can you name 10 things and say if singular or plural?

example.problem: Name 5 things, then their plurals
example.solution: Dog→dogs, ball→balls, tree→trees, book→books, pen→pens

slides.inSimpleWords: You are a Naming Word Expert!

slides.title: Mitthu Celebrates
slides.storyContext: Mitthu sings: You learned naming words! All types! Singular and plural! You are amazing, Arjun!
slides.inSimpleWords: You mastered naming words!

slides.title: All About Naming Words
slides.storyContext: Mitthu sits on the bench with Arjun. 'Naming words are words that name people, animals, places, and things. Arjun, Mitthu, dog, park, tree, ball — all naming words! They tell us what something is called!'

points.label: Naming words (nouns)
points.text: Name people, animals, places, things

points.label: Examples
points.text: Boy, girl, dog, cat, park, home, tree, ball, book

points.label: Singular and plural
points.text: One ball, two balls. Add 's' to make plural.

points.label: NOT naming words
points.text: Action words (jump, run) and describing words (happy, big) are NOT naming words.

slides.inSimpleWords: Naming words are the names of all things around us.

image.alt: All About Naming Words — Naming Words

subject: English
title: Arjun and Mitthu Play Games with Actions
hook: Learn action words — all the things we do!

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A playful parrot who shows all kinds of actions

slides.title: Arjun and Mitthu Play Games with Actions

image.alt: Arjun and Mitthu Play Games with Actions — Action Words

slides.title: Let's Play and Do Things!
slides.storyContext: Arjun wakes up ready to play. Mitthu flies into the room. 'Arjun! Let's do things today! Walk, run, jump, play — these are all action words! They tell us what we DO!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Action words are words for things we do.

image.alt: Let's Play and Do Things! — Action Words

slides.title: What is an Action Word?
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'An action word is a word that shows what someone or something DOES.'

points.label: Definition
points.text: An action word (verb) is a word that tells us what someone or something is doing, did, or will do.

points.label: Examples
points.text: Jump, walk, run, eat, play, sing, write, read, sleep — these are all ACTION words.

slides.inSimpleWords: Action words tell us what we DO.

image.alt: What is an Action Word? — Action Words

slides.title: Moving Actions
slides.storyContext: Arjun jumps out of bed. 'I jump!' He walks to the window. 'I walk!' He starts to run. 'I run!' Mitthu flies around his head. 'Jump, walk, run — moving actions! We use these verbs to show movement! Go, skip, hop, climb, roll — all moving actions!'

points.label: Moving actions
points.text: Jump, walk, run, skip, hop, climb, roll, swim

slides.inSimpleWords: Jump, walk, run, skip are moving actions.

slides.title: Different Ways to Move
slides.storyContext: Mitthu shows Arjun all the different ways to move. 'You can walk slowly. Skip happily. Hop on one foot. Climb up a tree. Swim in the water. Crawl on the ground!'

points.label: Slow moving
points.text: Walk, crawl, creep, slide, glide

points.label: Fast moving
points.text: Run, sprint, dash, rush, zoom

points.label: Up and down
points.text: Jump, hop, leap, climb, fly, swim, dive

example.problem: What action word means to move very fast?
example.solution: Run! Or sprint, dash, rush, zoom. All show fast moving.

slides.inSimpleWords: Many action words show different ways to move.

image.alt: Different Ways to Move — Action Words

slides.title: Eating and Drinking
slides.storyContext: At breakfast, Arjun sits down. 'I eat!' He puts toast in his mouth. Mitthu lands on his plate and pecks. 'I eat too!' Then Arjun drinks milk. 'I drink!' Mitthu sips water. 'Eat, drink, chew, taste — eating actions!'

points.label: Eating actions
points.text: Eat, drink, chew, taste, bite, swallow

points.label: More food actions
points.text: Cook, bake, boil, fry, mix, slice, cut, peel

example.problem: What action word means to take food into your mouth?
example.solution: Eat! Also: chew, bite, taste, swallow

slides.inSimpleWords: Eat and drink are eating actions.

slides.title: Food Actions Every Day
slides.storyContext: Arjun's mother cooks lunch. 'I chop, mix, boil, and fry!' Then at the table, Arjun says, 'I chew, taste, swallow, and drink!'

points.label: Cooking actions
points.text: Cook, bake, boil, fry, roast, grill, slice, mix

points.label: Eating actions
points.text: Eat, chew, bite, taste, swallow, sip, lick, munch

example.problem: What action word means to turn wheat into bread?
example.solution: Bake! Or grind, knead, bake — multiple actions in cooking.

slides.inSimpleWords: We use many action words when cooking and eating food.

image.alt: Food Actions Every Day — Action Words

slides.title: Sound Actions
slides.storyContext: After breakfast, Arjun sings happily. 'I sing!' His friend Ravi shouts from outside. 'Someone talks or shouts!' Mitthu chirps. 'Sing, talk, shout, laugh, cry — sound actions! We make these sounds with our voice!'

points.label: Sound actions
points.text: Sing, talk, shout, laugh, cry, whisper, call

slides.inSimpleWords: Sing, talk, shout are sound actions.

slides.title: Talking and Listening
slides.storyContext: Mitthu says, 'Talk, listen, hear, whisper, shout, yell—these are sound actions with your voice or ears!'

points.label: Voice actions
points.text: Talk, speak, shout, whisper, yell, sing, hum, murmur

points.label: Sound actions
points.text: Listen, hear, beep, ring, buzz, bang, crash, boom

example.problem: What action word means to make a loud sound with your voice?
example.solution: Shout! Or yell, call, scream. These are loud voice actions.

slides.inSimpleWords: Many action words show different sounds we make or hear.

slides.title: Daily Actions
slides.storyContext: At school, Arjun writes his name carefully. 'I write!' His teacher reads from a book. 'Teacher reads!' On the playground, children play. 'We play!' Mitthu watches. 'Write, read, play, draw, color, count — all daily actions at school!'

points.label: School actions
points.text: Write, read, draw, color, count, learn, teach, play

points.label: More school actions
points.text: Listen, answer, ask, solve, erase, copy, paste, paint

example.problem: What action word means to make pictures with pencil?
example.solution: Draw! Also: color, paint, sketch

slides.inSimpleWords: Write, read, draw, and play are daily actions.

slides.title: Learning at School
slides.storyContext: Arjun's day is full of actions. 'I listen to my teacher. I write in my notebook. I read my book. I solve math problems. I play with friends. I eat lunch. I go home.'

points.label: Learning actions
points.text: Listen, learn, study, read, write, solve, answer, ask

points.label: Creative actions
points.text: Draw, paint, color, create, build, make, design, sketch

example.problem: What are three action words a teacher does?
example.solution: Teach, explain, help (or: write, read, show, ask)

slides.inSimpleWords: School is full of different action words every day.

slides.title: Feeling and Thinking
slides.storyContext: At the zoo, Arjun sees the lion. 'I'm scared!' Mitthu sees shiny mangoes. 'I like mangoes!' Arjun thinks about what to buy. 'I think!' Mitthu smiles. 'Like, love, fear, think, know, understand, wish — these are feeling and thinking actions!'

points.label: Feeling actions
points.text: Like, love, fear, think, know, feel, understand, hope, wish

slides.inSimpleWords: Think, like, love, know are thinking actions.

slides.title: Emotions and Thoughts
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains the difference between what we DO externally and what happens inside our minds and hearts.

points.label: Feeling actions
points.text: Love, like, hate, fear, enjoy, prefer, desire, wish

points.label: Thinking actions
points.text: Think, know, understand, believe, remember, forget, imagine, wonder

points.label: Mood actions
points.text: Smile, frown, laugh, cry, worry, hope, dream, doubt

example.problem: What action word means to picture something in your mind?
example.solution: Imagine! Also: dream, think, believe, wonder

slides.inSimpleWords: Feeling and thinking are action words too, even though we can't always see them.

slides.title: Action Game
slides.storyContext: Mitthu starts a game. 'I'll do an action. You name the word!' Mitthu jumps. 'Jump!' Mitthu runs around. 'Run!' Mitthu eats a seed. 'Eat!' Arjun laughs. 'I understand! Everything we DO is an action word!'

points.label: Action word test
points.text: Can you name what the action is?

example.problem: What action word means to close your eyes and rest?
example.solution: Sleep! Also: rest, nap, doze

slides.inSimpleWords: Everything we do has an action word.

slides.title: Can YOU Do This Action?
slides.storyContext: Mitthu challenges Arjun: 'Can you jump? Can you run? Can you sit? Can you stand? Can you smile? Can you think? Show me the action!'

points.label: Easy actions
points.text: Sit, stand, walk, run, jump, clap, blink, smile

points.label: Harder to see
points.text: Think, listen, remember, imagine, believe, hope, feel

example.problem: Which of these is an action word? Dream, table, happy, read
example.solution: Dream and read are action words. Table is a thing. Happy is a feeling-word, not an action word.

slides.inSimpleWords: Some action words we can see. Some happen inside us that we can't see.

image.alt: Can YOU Do This Action? — Action Words

slides.title: Night Actions
slides.storyContext: The sun sets. Arjun yawns. 'I sleep now!' Mitthu settles on a branch. 'I rest!' Before bed, Arjun's mom hugs him. 'I love you!' Mitthu chirps. 'Sleep, rest, hug, kiss, dream — night and love actions! Every moment has an action word!'

points.label: More actions
points.text: Sleep, rest, dream, hug, kiss, love, help, care

slides.inSimpleWords: Sleep, hug, and love are actions we do.

slides.title: Present, Past, and Future Actions
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches Arjun how action words change with time. 'I jump NOW. I jumped YESTERDAY. I will jump TOMORROW!'

points.label: Present tense (now)
points.text: Jump, run, walk, eat, read, write, play, sleep (happening right now)

points.label: Past tense (already happened)
points.text: Jumped, ran, walked, ate, read, wrote, played, slept (usually add 'ed')

points.label: Future tense (will happen)
points.text: Will jump, will run, will walk, will eat (use 'will' before the action)

example.problem: Fill in the blanks: I ___ (play) yesterday. I ___ (play) now. I will ___ (play) tomorrow.
example.solution: I played yesterday. I play now. I will play tomorrow.

slides.inSimpleWords: Action words change when we talk about past, present, or future.

image.alt: Present, Past, and Future Actions — Action Words

slides.title: Action Words Change Over Time
slides.storyContext: Mitthu shows Arjun how one action word changes. 'I run now. I ran yesterday. I will run tomorrow. Same action, different time!'

points.label: Now (present)
points.text: Run, eat, play, read, jump, sing, write, draw

points.label: Then (past)
points.text: Ran, ate, played, read, jumped, sang, wrote, drew

points.label: Later (future)
points.text: Will run, will eat, will play, will read, will jump, will sing, will write, will draw

example.problem: Write the past tense of: eat, go, see, run
example.solution: Ate, went, saw, ran (these are irregular—they change completely!)

slides.inSimpleWords: Most action words add 'ed' for past. Some change completely!

image.alt: Action Words Change Over Time — Action Words

slides.title: Actions Throughout the Day
slides.storyContext: Mitthu makes a timeline: 'Morning: wake, eat, get dressed. School: learn, read, write, play. Evening: eat, help, sleep. So many actions!'

points.label: Different times
points.text: Morning: wake, wash, eat. Day: learn, play, read. Night: rest, sleep, dream

example.problem: List 5 actions YOU do at school.
example.solution: Learn, read, write, play, listen (or similar)

slides.inSimpleWords: Every part of the day has action words!

image.alt: Actions Throughout the Day — Action Words

slides.title: Continuous Actions (-ing)
slides.storyContext: Mitthu shows: 'Look! I'm jumping NOW. I'm running NOW. Add 'ing' to show it's happening right now!'

points.label: Make present continuous
points.text: Jump→jumping, run→running, eat→eating, play→playing, read→reading

example.problem: Add 'ing': play, eat, run, sing, write
example.solution: Playing, eating, running, singing, writing

slides.inSimpleWords: Add 'ing' for actions happening right now.

slides.title: Action Words in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches: 'I jump. You walk. He runs. She sings. We play. They sleep. Each sentence shows an action!'

points.label: Subject + action
points.text: I run. You jump. He eats. She reads. We play. They sleep.

example.problem: Make 3 sentences using different action words and people.
example.solution: I eat. The dog runs. She reads. (any correct sentences)

slides.inSimpleWords: Use action words to describe what people do.

image.alt: Action Words in Sentences — Action Words

slides.title: All Action Word Skills
slides.storyContext: Mitthu asks: 'Can you: name an action, say its past tense, make it continuous, and use it in a sentence?'

points.label: Example: run
points.text: Action: run, Past: ran, Continuous: running, Sentence: 'I am running.'

example.problem: For 'play': write present, past, continuous, and a sentence.
example.solution: Play, played, playing, 'I play at school.'

slides.inSimpleWords: You now know so much about action words!

image.alt: All Action Word Skills — Action Words

slides.title: Action Speed Challenge
slides.storyContext: Mitthu calls out: Eat! Jump! Sing! Read! Arjun shouts back: Action word!
slides.inSimpleWords: You know action words!

slides.title: All Action Words You Use
slides.storyContext: Mitthu makes a list of common actions.

points.label: Every day
points.text: Walk, run, eat, drink, read, write, play, learn, sleep, rest, think, love

slides.inSimpleWords: These actions you use constantly!

slides.title: Verb Master Test
slides.storyContext: Give past, present, and ing form for any action word!

example.problem: For run, eat, play give all three forms
example.solution: Run: ran/running, Eat: ate/eating, Play: played/playing

slides.inSimpleWords: You master action words!

slides.title: Arjun is Amazing
slides.storyContext: Mitthu: You know all action words! Moving, eating, talking, thinking! You can describe anything now!
slides.inSimpleWords: You are an expert!

slides.title: All Kinds of Actions
slides.storyContext: Mitthu sits on the headboard as Arjun drifts to sleep. 'Action words tell us what we DO. Move, eat, talk, read, play, think, feel, sleep — all actions! Everything we do has an action word!'

points.label: Action words (verbs)
points.text: Tell us what we do, feel, think, or say

points.label: All kinds
points.text: Moving, eating, talking, reading, playing, thinking, feeling, sleeping

points.label: Time changes words
points.text: Play (now), played (past), will play (future)

points.label: Some we see, some hidden
points.text: Run and jump we can see. Think and feel happen inside.

slides.inSimpleWords: Action words tell us what we do, say, or feel.

subject: Biology
title: Life Processes: The Story of Nutrition, Respiration & Transport
hook: Meet Arjun, a farm boy discovering how living things stay alive through food, oxygen, and heartbeats.

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: village health worker explaining the body

slides.title: Life Processes
slides.storyContext: Arjun watches the sunrise over his family's farm and wonders: what keeps people and plants alive every single day?

slides.title: The Farm Awakens
slides.storyContext: Arjun sees his grandmother eating parathas at dawn, his water buffalo drinking from the well, and the crops turning green in the rain. He asks Priya: 'How does eating make us strong? Why do we breathe? How does food reach every part of our body?' Priya smiles and begins.

slides.title: What is Nutrition?
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: 'Food is fuel, Arjun. Just as your farm needs seeds and water to grow, your body needs nutrients to build and repair itself.'

points.label: Definition
points.text: Nutrition is the process of taking in food and using it for energy, growth, and repair.

points.label: Autotrophic nutrition
points.text: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis (light + CO₂ + water → glucose + O₂). Leaves contain chlorophyll.

points.label: Heterotrophic nutrition
points.text: Animals eat organic matter. Humans have holozoic nutrition: ingestion → digestion → absorption → assimilation → egestion.

example.problem: A plant sits in sunlight for 6 hours with water and CO₂ available. What does it produce?
example.solution: Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) and oxygen (O₂). The plant uses chlorophyll to capture light energy.

slides.inSimpleWords: Plants make food from sun, water, and air. Animals eat plants or other animals to get energy.

slides.title: Photosynthesis in the Fields
slides.storyContext: Arjun watches his crops in the morning sun. Priya points to the green leaves. 'Those leaves are tiny food factories! They capture sunlight and turn it into food for the plant. That's photosynthesis!'

image.alt: Photosynthesis in the Fields — Life Processes

slides.title: Photosynthesis Formula and Process
slides.storyContext: Priya writes the equation in the sand: '6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂'

points.label: The equation
points.text: Carbon dioxide + Water + Light → Glucose + Oxygen

points.label: Light reactions (thylakoid)
points.text: Light energy absorbed by chlorophyll → electrons excited → ATP and NADPH produced → O₂ released

points.label: Dark reactions / Calvin cycle (stroma)
points.text: CO₂ fixed by RuBP enzyme → 3-PG → uses ATP and NADPH → produces glucose

example.problem: Why do plants need light? Why do they need water and CO₂?
example.solution: Light provides energy. Water and CO₂ are the raw materials. Together they make glucose (food) and release O₂.

slides.inSimpleWords: Plants use light energy to turn water and air into food. They release oxygen that we breathe.

image.alt: Photosynthesis Formula and Process — Life Processes

slides.title: Digestion in Humans
slides.storyContext: Arjun eats fresh bajra roti and asks Priya where it goes. 'Let me trace the journey,' she says, pointing to her mouth, stomach, and small intestine.

points.label: Mouth
points.text: Saliva contains amylase enzyme, which begins breaking down starch into sugars. Teeth mechanically crush food.

points.label: Stomach
points.text: Gastric juice (HCl + pepsin) breaks down proteins. Food becomes a semi-liquid paste called chyme.

points.label: Small intestine
points.text: Pancreatic enzymes digest carbs, fats, and proteins. Bile emulsifies fats. Nutrients are absorbed into the blood through villi.

example.problem: You eat a chapati with butter and dal. Name the major nutrients and which part of the digestive system breaks them down.
example.solution: Carbs (chapati) → amylase in mouth and pancreas. Protein (dal) → pepsin in stomach. Fat (butter) → lipase in small intestine.

slides.inSimpleWords: Your mouth chews food, your stomach churns it, and your small intestine absorbs the useful nutrients into your blood.

slides.title: From Mouth to Intestine
slides.storyContext: Priya traces the path of food inside Arjun's body. 'Bite, swallow, squeeze—your food travels down the esophagus like a slide. Then it's churned in the stomach. Finally it moves to the small intestine where the real magic happens!'

image.alt: From Mouth to Intestine — Life Processes

slides.title: Digestion Enzymes and Steps
slides.storyContext: Priya draws out the timeline of digestion with each enzyme's role.

points.label: Enzyme breakdown
points.text: Amylase (carbs) → Protease (proteins) → Lipase (fats) → Nuclease (nucleic acids)

points.label: Nutrient absorption
points.text: Glucose, amino acids, fatty acids, glycerol, vitamins, minerals absorbed in small intestine via villi into capillaries

points.label: Egestion
points.text: Undigested material (fiber, dead cells) moves to large intestine, water reabsorbed, waste stored as feces

example.problem: Why do villi in the small intestine have a huge surface area and lots of capillaries?
example.solution: Large surface area absorbs more nutrients. Capillaries transport absorbed nutrients into the bloodstream for distribution.

slides.inSimpleWords: Enzymes are tiny helpers that break down food into pieces small enough to enter the blood.

image.alt: Digestion Enzymes and Steps — Life Processes

slides.title: Respiration: Aerobic & Anaerobic
slides.storyContext: After lunch, Arjun runs to the field. His breathing quickens. Priya asks: 'Do you know why your cells need oxygen, even when you rest?'

points.label: Aerobic respiration
points.text: In the presence of oxygen: Glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + Energy (38 ATP). Occurs in mitochondria. Most efficient.

points.label: Anaerobic respiration
points.text: Without oxygen: Glucose → Lactic acid + Energy (2 ATP) in muscles. Glucose → Ethanol + CO₂ + Energy in yeast.

points.label: Why respiration?
points.text: Every cell needs ATP (energy) to work—pumping ions, contracting muscles, synthesizing proteins, maintaining body temperature.

example.problem: You sprint in a race. Your muscles suddenly feel exhausted and burn. Why does this happen?
example.solution: During intense exercise, your muscles consume oxygen faster than the blood can supply it. They switch to anaerobic respiration, producing lactic acid, which causes the burn and fatigue.

slides.inSimpleWords: Your cells burn glucose with oxygen to make energy. Without oxygen, they make energy slower and produce lactic acid (the burn you feel).

slides.title: Why We Breathe
slides.storyContext: Arjun breathes deeply after running. Priya says, 'Every breath brings oxygen to your blood. Your blood carries it to billions of cells. Each cell uses oxygen to release energy from food. Then carbon dioxide goes back to your lungs to breathe out.'

slides.title: Aerobic Respiration Stages
slides.storyContext: Priya explains that aerobic respiration has stages: Glycolysis → Krebs cycle → Electron transport chain.

points.label: Glycolysis (cytoplasm)
points.text: Glucose (6C) → Pyruvate (3C) + 2 ATP + 2 NADH. Does NOT need oxygen.

points.label: Krebs cycle (mitochondrial matrix)
points.text: Pyruvate + Acetyl-CoA → CO₂ + NADH + FADH₂ + ATP. Completes glucose breakdown.

points.label: Electron transport chain (inner mitochondrial membrane)
points.text: NADH and FADH₂ → 32-34 ATP + H₂O. Oxygen is final electron acceptor.

example.problem: Why is aerobic respiration much more efficient (38 ATP) than anaerobic (2 ATP)?
example.solution: Aerobic uses three stages to extract energy. Anaerobic only does glycolysis (partial breakdown), releasing little energy. In aerobic, oxygen accepting electrons in ETC generates most ATP.

slides.inSimpleWords: Aerobic respiration breaks down glucose completely with oxygen, making a LOT of energy (38 ATP per glucose).

slides.title: Transport in Humans: The Circulatory System
slides.storyContext: Grandpa Hari places Arjun's hand on his chest. 'Feel that? That is your heart pumping blood to every corner of your body, delivering oxygen and nutrients.'

points.label: The heart
points.text: A muscular four-chambered organ. Right side pumps deoxygenated blood to lungs. Left side pumps oxygenated blood to the body.

points.label: Blood vessels
points.text: Arteries carry blood away from heart (high pressure). Veins carry blood back (low pressure). Capillaries exchange gases and nutrients with cells.

points.label: Blood composition
points.text: RBCs carry oxygen via hemoglobin. WBCs fight infection. Platelets clot. Plasma carries nutrients, hormones, waste.

example.problem: Trace the path of oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the leg muscles and back.
example.solution: Lungs → Pulmonary veins → Left atrium → Left ventricle → Aorta → Femoral artery → Leg capillaries (oxygen released to muscles) → Femoral vein → Vena cava → Right atrium.

slides.inSimpleWords: Your heart is a pump. It pushes blood through arteries carrying oxygen to all your cells, and veins bring blood back to the lungs to get fresh oxygen.

image.alt: Transport in Humans: The Circulatory System — Life Processes

slides.title: The Heartbeat
slides.storyContext: Arjun feels his own heartbeat. 'Lub-dub, lub-dub!' Grandpa explains, 'That's your heart contracting—squeezing blood out. Then it relaxes to fill with more blood. Your heart never stops, Arjun, not even while you sleep!'

slides.title: Heart Chambers and Valves
slides.storyContext: Priya draws the heart with its four chambers and shows how valves prevent backflow.

points.label: Right atrium
points.text: Receives deoxygenated blood from body via superior and inferior vena cava

points.label: Right ventricle
points.text: Pumps deoxygenated blood to lungs via pulmonary artery

points.label: Left atrium
points.text: Receives oxygenated blood from lungs via pulmonary veins

points.label: Left ventricle
points.text: Pumps oxygenated blood to body via aorta. Has thickest walls.

example.problem: Why does the left ventricle have thicker muscular walls than the right?
example.solution: The left ventricle must pump blood to the entire body at high pressure. The right only pumps to nearby lungs at lower pressure.

slides.inSimpleWords: The heart has four chambers working together like a double pump—one side for lungs, one side for the body.

image.alt: Heart Chambers and Valves — Life Processes

slides.title: Blood's Journey
slides.storyContext: Priya uses a red thread to trace blood's path: 'Body → heart → lungs → heart → body again. Around and around, oxygen and nutrients going out, waste coming back.'

slides.title: Blood Composition and Function
slides.storyContext: Priya looks at a drop of blood under the microscope. 'Blood isn't just red liquid. It has red cells, white cells, platelets, and plasma—each with a job!'

points.label: Red blood cells (RBCs)
points.text: Contain hemoglobin (iron-protein). Carry O₂ from lungs to cells. Carry CO₂ from cells to lungs. Lifespan ~120 days.

points.label: White blood cells (WBCs)
points.text: Fight infection and pathogens. Types: neutrophils (bacteria), lymphocytes (immune memory), macrophages (clean up debris).

points.label: Platelets + Plasma
points.text: Platelets form blood clots. Plasma carries nutrients, hormones, antibodies, waste. 55% of blood volume.

example.problem: Why does a person with anemia feel tired even after rest?
example.solution: Fewer RBCs or less hemoglobin means less oxygen reaches cells. Cells can't make enough ATP, causing fatigue.

slides.inSimpleWords: Blood is a mix of cells and liquid. Red cells carry oxygen. White cells fight germs. Platelets stop bleeding.

image.alt: Blood Composition and Function — Life Processes

slides.title: Excretion: Removing Waste
slides.storyContext: Priya says: 'After your cells use nutrients and oxygen, they produce waste. Your kidneys clean the blood like a water filter in your home.'

points.label: What is excretion?
points.text: The removal of metabolic waste (urea, uric acid, excess salts, excess water) from the body.

points.label: The nephron
points.text: Functional unit of the kidney. Has Bowman's capsule (filtration), loop of Henle (reabsorption of water and salts), and collecting duct (urine formation).

points.label: Other excretory organs
points.text: Lungs excrete CO₂ and water vapor. Skin excretes water and salts as sweat. Liver produces urea.

example.problem: A person drinks 3 liters of water but only produces 1.5 liters of urine. Where did the extra water go?
example.solution: The kidneys reabsorb excess water in the loop of Henle and collecting duct. This water re-enters the bloodstream. Extra water is also lost through sweat and breathing (evaporation).

slides.inSimpleWords: Your kidneys filter waste and extra water from your blood to make urine. They also reabsorb useful water and salts back into your blood.

slides.title: Urine Formation
slides.storyContext: Priya explains the three steps: 'Blood enters the kidney. Useful stuff gets filtered into a tube. Then useful stuff gets reabsorbed back into the blood. What's left becomes urine.'

slides.title: Nephron Function in Detail
slides.storyContext: Priya maps out the filtration process step by step.

points.label: Ultrafiltration (Bowman's capsule)
points.text: Blood pressure forces small molecules (glucose, ions, urea, water) through capillary wall. Large molecules (proteins, RBCs) stay in blood.

points.label: Selective reabsorption (loop of Henle + proximal tubule)
points.text: Useful glucose and ions reabsorbed back into capillaries. Water follows osmotically. Happens at Loop of Henle and collecting duct.

points.label: Tubular secretion + Urine storage
points.text: Extra ions, ammonia, drugs secreted into tubule. Final urine (urea, excess water, excess ions) moves to bladder.

example.problem: Why is glucose present in normal urine unusual? What does it suggest?
example.solution: Normally, all glucose is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule. Glucose in urine suggests blood glucose is too high (diabetes) or kidney damage.

slides.inSimpleWords: Kidneys filter waste but bring back useful things—glucose and water. Urine is just the waste and extra water.

image.alt: Nephron Function in Detail — Life Processes

slides.title: Full Example: A Day in Arjun's Life
slides.storyContext: Arjun eats breakfast, works in the field, and returns home tired. Let's trace what happens inside his body.

example.problem: Arjun eats a plate of rice and beans at 7 AM, then works for 4 hours in the hot sun. Describe the life processes happening in his body.
example.solution: Digestion: In the mouth, saliva breaks down rice starch. In the stomach, gastric juice digests bean proteins. In the small intestine, glucose and amino acids are absorbed. Respiration: Glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + energy (ATP) in his muscle cells, providing energy for work. Transport: His heart pumps oxygen-rich blood through arteries to muscles and brain. Deoxygenated blood returns via veins. Excretion: His kidneys filter urea from the breakdown of amino acids. His skin sweats to cool him and excrete excess salt and water. His lungs exhale CO₂.

image.alt: Full Example: A Day in Arjun's Life — Life Processes

slides.title: All Life Processes at Once
slides.storyContext: Priya summarizes: 'Every second, your body is doing all five life processes together. Nutrition brings in fuel. Respiration releases energy. Transport delivers it everywhere. Excretion removes waste. And growth happens from it all!'

example.problem: A plant grows in sunlight. Describe all the life processes it is performing simultaneously.
example.solution: Nutrition: Photosynthesis (leaves make glucose). Respiration: Mitochondria burn some glucose for growth energy. Transport: Phloem carries glucose, xylem carries water and minerals from roots. Excretion: Stomata release O₂ and excess water vapor. Growth: Cells divide and expand using energy and nutrients.

image.alt: All Life Processes at Once — Life Processes

slides.title: Challenge: The Athlete's Question
slides.storyContext: Arjun's older cousin Vikram trains for a cricket match. He asks: 'During the match, I run hard for 30 seconds but feel exhausted even though I keep breathing. Why?'

example.problem: During intense cricket sprints lasting 30 seconds, muscle cells cannot get oxygen fast enough. What type of respiration do they use? What waste is produced? Why does Vikram feel the burn?
example.solution: His muscle cells switch to anaerobic respiration: Glucose → Lactic acid + 2 ATP. Though this produces only 2 ATP per glucose (vs. 38 in aerobic respiration), it provides quick energy. However, lactic acid accumulates, lowering muscle pH and causing the sensation of burn and temporary fatigue. After the sprint, increased breathing (oxygen debt) helps convert lactic acid back to glucose.

image.alt: Challenge: The Athlete's Question — Life Processes

slides.title: Challenge: The High-Altitude Question
slides.storyContext: Arjun's friend Rohan travels to the mountains where the air is thin. He asks: 'Why do I feel tired and breathe harder up here? Is my body still respiring the same way?'

example.problem: At high altitude, atmospheric oxygen is lower. Explain how this affects aerobic respiration, red blood cell production, and breathing rate.
example.solution: Lower O₂ pressure → less oxygen diffuses into blood → cells produce less ATP aerobically. Body compensates: breathing rate increases to pull in more air; kidneys produce erythropoietin (EPO) to stimulate RBC production. This adaptation takes days. Without it, cells rely partly on anaerobic respiration (lactic acid buildup), causing fatigue and shortness of breath.

image.alt: Challenge: The High-Altitude Question — Life Processes

slides.title: Plant vs Animal Nutrition
slides.storyContext: Arjun watches his crops grow. 'Plants don't move. They use sun and air to make food. But I must move to find food to eat. Different life processes!'

points.label: Plants
points.text: Make own food via photosynthesis. Don't move. Use light, water, CO₂.

points.label: Animals
points.text: Must find and eat food. Move to hunt or gather. Digest it for energy.

example.problem: Why do plants need sunlight but animals need to eat food?
example.solution: Plants make food from light (photosynthesis). Animals can't make food—they must eat it.

slides.inSimpleWords: Plants and animals use different nutrition methods.

image.alt: Plant vs Animal Nutrition — Life Processes

slides.title: All Processes Now
slides.storyContext: Priya: Right now, you digest, breathe, pump blood, excrete waste, and grow! Five processes at once!

slides.title: Swimming Challenge
slides.storyContext: What happens in your body during hard swimming?

example.problem: All 5 processes during 5-minute swim
example.solution: Nutrition: breakfast fuel. Respiration: aerobic + lactic. Transport: oxygen delivery. Excretion: CO2, sweat. Growth: muscles repair.

slides.title: The Miracle of Life
slides.storyContext: Priya: Life processes never stop, Arjun. In plants, animals, you. Birth to death. That is the miracle.

slides.title: Summary: Life Processes Keep You Alive
slides.storyContext: Priya concludes: 'Arjun, now you understand—every bite of food, every breath, every heartbeat is your body's way of staying alive.'

points.label: Nutrition
points.text: Plants use photosynthesis (autotrophic); animals digest food (heterotrophic) to extract nutrients.

points.label: Digestion
points.text: Mouth → stomach → small intestine. Enzymes break down food; nutrients are absorbed into blood.

points.label: Respiration
points.text: Aerobic (with O₂) produces 38 ATP per glucose. Anaerobic (without O₂) produces 2 ATP.

points.label: Transport
points.text: Heart pumps blood through arteries and veins, delivering O₂ and nutrients; capillaries exchange with cells.

points.label: Excretion
points.text: Kidneys filter urea and water; lungs excrete CO₂; skin excretes sweat; liver produces urea.

image.alt: Summary: Life Processes Keep You Alive — Life Processes
